name: Follow AESO dispatches and directives
summary: The AESO tells each offered asset how much to generate by issuing dispatches in its ADaMS system whenever the system price crosses the asset's offer blocks, so the company's real-time desk receives thousands of dispatches a month. The trader on shift acknowledges each one, checks it against the offer, and passes it to the gas control room, the hydro control centre or the renewables operations centre, whose operators ramp the unit, hold it inside the allowed variance and report problems. The work is minutes long but continuous, bunches up in volatile and cold-weather hours, and late acknowledgements or poor delivery are among the most frequent ISO rule matters reviewed by the market surveillance administrator.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with three converted gas units, partner unit shares, about ten offered hydro assets and a 10 MW battery, dispatched through a 24-hour real-time desk.
baseline.notes: Rules as in force in 2019-2022: section 201.7 acknowledgement, section 203.4 (2020 text) delivery, operating reserve directives under division 205. ADaMS was the dispatch system.

trigger: The AESO system controller issues a dispatch or directive for one of the company's assets in ADaMS.
end_state: The dispatch is acknowledged, the asset is delivering the dispatched MW inside the allowable variance (or a restatement or start-up has been handed on), and the dispatch is logged.

volume.seasonality: Highest in winter and on high-wind, high-volatility days when prices cross many offer blocks; lowest in mild shoulder months.

evidence.note: Organisation file driver dd_dispatches: about 15 dispatchable offered assets each receiving several dispatches a day. Not checked against AESO data.

surge.cause: winter cold snaps with tight supply

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file: cold snaps raise demand and price volatility, so assets move up and down the merit order more often; estimate.
About 100 dispatches a day at about 5 minutes of desk time each; roughly one of the two staffed desk seats.
Ramping and holding converted units on target.
Allocating and monitoring hydro output.
Battery setpoints and occasional wind curtailments.

systems.name: AESO Automated Dispatch and Messaging System (ADaMS)
AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
Energy trading and risk management system
Hydro, wind and battery SCADA and remote control
Recorded desk and control room phone lines

resources.name: Gas-fired steam unit converted from coal (about 400 to 460 MW)
Hydro plant with dam and reservoir

steps.name: AESO issues a dispatch
steps.description: The AESO system controller issues a dispatch to one of the company's assets in ADaMS, naming the asset, Dispatch On or Off, the MW level and the time it takes effect, as the system marginal price moves through the asset's offer blocks.

evidence.note: Dispatch content as listed in 2012-005R section 2.

steps.name: ADaMS alerts the desk
steps.description: The ADaMS dispatch pane on the real-time desk flashes and sounds an alert for the new dispatch, and the dispatch is time-stamped in the AESO system and in the desk's dispatch history for later settlement and compliance checks.

evidence.note: ADaMS dispatch pane described in 2012-005R; alert behaviour is an estimate.

steps.name: Acknowledge the dispatch
steps.description: The real-time trader on shift reads the dispatch and clicks the Ack Disp button in the ADaMS dispatch pane, which tells the AESO the dispatch was received; during busy hours several dispatches may be waiting at once.

error.defect_description: Dispatch acknowledged late or not at all during a busy period.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 201.7 s.5: acknowledge receipt of a dispatch

evidence.note: Acknowledgement duty in 201.7 s.5 as cited in 2012-005R; 67 section 201.7 matters market-wide in 2021 (MSA). The error rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Check the dispatch against the offer
steps.description: The trader compares the dispatch MW and time with the asset's current offer blocks, available capability, ramp rate and any reserve award, to spot a dispatch that the asset cannot follow or that conflicts with a pending restatement.

next.condition: energy dispatch to a converted gas or cogeneration unit
energy dispatch to a hydro asset
dispatch to the battery or a wind farm curtailment
dispatch needs a unit start or shutdown
dispatch looks inconsistent with the offer or capability

evidence.note: Branch shares follow the organisation file's dispatchable assets (more hydro assets than gas units); estimates.

steps.name: Relay the dispatch to the gas control room
steps.description: The trader phones the converted unit's control room on the recorded line, or confirms the operator has seen the dispatch on the ADaMS display there, and gives the MW target, the effective time and any reserve the unit must keep.

error.defect_description: MW target misheard or wrong unit named.

evidence.note: Relay practice is an estimate for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Ramp the gas unit
steps.description: The control room operator enters the new load target in the distributed control system, adjusts burners, fans and feedwater as the unit moves at its offered ramp rate, and starts the move within ten minutes of the dispatch time but not before it.

error.defect_description: Ramp started late or overshoots the target.

control.basis: Plant operating procedures and boiler and turbine limits under a certificated shift engineer: dispatch is followed only within safe ramp rates and equipment limits

evidence.note: Start within 10 minutes and ramp-time limits from 203.4 s.4; operator times and unit occupancy are estimates.

steps.name: Hold the gas unit on target
steps.description: The operator watches the unit settle at the dispatched MW and keeps the 10-minute average output inside the allowable dispatch variance, telling the desk at once if a mill, pump or burner problem stops the unit from reaching or holding the target.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.3 and s.4: start moving within 10 minutes of the dispatch time, reach steady state within the ramp-time limit and stay inside the allowable dispatch variance

evidence.note: Steady-state and variance obligations from 203.4 s.3 and s.4(2); times are estimates.

steps.name: Relay the dispatch to hydro control
steps.description: The trader passes the dispatch to the hydro control centre by phone or by the shared ADaMS display, with the plant or river system, the MW target and the effective time.

error.defect_description: Target given for the wrong plant.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Set hydro units to the target
steps.description: The hydro control centre operator spreads the MW across units and plants in the river system on SCADA, keeping within the water schedule, licence minimum flows and forebay limits, and starts or stops units remotely where needed.

error.defect_description: Allocation breaks a flow limit downstream.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.3 and s.4: start moving within 10 minutes of the dispatch time, reach steady state within the ramp-time limit and stay inside the allowable dispatch variance

evidence.note: Delivery obligations from 203.4; hydro allocation practice and times are estimates.

steps.name: Monitor hydro output and river flows
steps.description: The operator watches plant output against the dispatch and the downstream flows and levels, correcting unit loadings when a plant drifts outside the dispatch variance or a river limit is approached.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Set the battery or wind farm setpoint
steps.description: The renewables operations centre operator sets the battery's charge or discharge setpoint, or a wind farm's curtailment limit, in SCADA to match the dispatch, and checks the battery's state of charge can sustain the instruction.

error.defect_description: Setpoint applied to the wrong asset or not released after the dispatch ends.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.3 and s.4: start moving within 10 minutes of the dispatch time, reach steady state within the ramp-time limit and stay inside the allowable dispatch variance

evidence.note: Storage must meet the 203.4 ramping and plus or minus 5 MW tolerance (2012-005R section 6); times and the battery occupancy are estimates.

steps.name: Relay an operating reserve directive
steps.description: The trader receives an AESO directive to convert awarded spinning or supplemental reserve into energy after a system contingency, passes it to the plant holding the reserve and tracks that the MW are delivered within the required time.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 205.2 directives and sections 205.5 and 205.6 spinning and supplemental reserve performance standards

next.condition: reserve held on a gas unit

evidence.note: Concurrent energy and reserve directives in 203.4 s.7; reserve delivery rules 205.5 and 205.6 had 69 matters in 2021. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Hand a start or shutdown to the plant
steps.description: When a dispatch requires a converted unit to start, synchronise or come off line, the trader calls the plant shift supervisor, agrees the start-up plan and verbal plan to the AESO, and hands the case to the plant's start and stop procedure.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.6(1)(b): verbal plan to the ISO when ramping to minimum stable generation

evidence.note: Verbal plan rule in 203.4 s.6(1)(b)(iii) and 2012-005R section 5; times are estimates.

steps.name: Query the dispatch with the AESO
steps.description: The trader phones the AESO system controller about a dispatch that does not match the asset's offer or restated capability, explains the asset's position and asks whether the dispatch stands or will be reissued.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: AESO confirms or reissues
steps.description: The AESO system controller checks the merit order and either confirms the dispatch or issues a corrected one in ADaMS, after which the desk checks it again before passing it on.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check delivery against the dispatch
steps.description: The trader watches the asset's real-time output on the historian and the AESO display and confirms it reached the dispatched MW within the ramp-time limit and is holding inside the allowable dispatch variance.

error.defect_description: A slow drift outside the variance is not noticed.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.2(2): dispatch protocols, personnel and software able to detect and address errors in a timely fashion

evidence.note: 203.4 s.2(2) requires such protocols; the deviation share is an estimate set against 83 section 203.4 matters market-wide in 2021 (MSA).

steps.name: Resolve a delivery deviation
steps.description: The trader calls the plant for the cause of the deviation; if the asset cannot recover within 20 minutes the trader starts a restatement of its capability, otherwise the trader records the cause and time the asset returned to target.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.4 s.5(1): restate within 20 minutes when an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or more

evidence.note: 20-minute rule in 203.4 s.5(1); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Log the dispatch
steps.description: The trader records the dispatch, acknowledgement time, ramp completion and any deviation or start-up hand-off in the desk dispatch log, which feeds the settlement check and the compliance file.

evidence.note: Estimate; many desks captured ADaMS history automatically and logged only exceptions by hand.

exceptions.name: Delivery deviation
exceptions.description: The asset does not reach or hold the dispatched MW; the trader finds the cause and restates capability if it will last 20 minutes or more.

exceptions.name: Dispatch queried with the AESO
exceptions.description: The dispatch conflicts with the offer or a pending restatement and the trader calls the system controller, who confirms or reissues it.

exceptions.name: Start or shutdown required
exceptions.description: The dispatch needs a converted unit to start or come off line, which is handed to the plant's start and stop procedure.

exceptions.name: Reserve directive after a contingency
exceptions.description: The AESO directs awarded spinning or supplemental reserve to deliver energy; the plant holding it must respond within the reserve performance standard.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from dispatch issue to logged delivery
benchmarks.population: Energy dispatches to an Alberta generator, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Derived from 203.4 s.4(2): up to 10 minutes to start plus ramp time plus 40 percent (at least 5 minutes); a 50 MW move at 5 to 10 MW a minute reaches steady state in about 20 to 30 minutes. Not a measured figure.

benchmarks.unit: MW either side of the dispatch (assets of 200 MW or less)
benchmarks.population: AESO stand-alone storage and generating units

evidence.note: 10 MW for assets above 200 MW.

benchmarks.unit: ISO rules compliance matters addressed, all Alberta participants

pain_points.description: Dispatches arrive continuously and bunch up in volatile hours, when the same trader is also taking restatement calls, so acknowledgements and deviation checks slip.

evidence.note: Dispatch acknowledgement (201.7) and delivery (203.4) were among the most frequent ISO rule matters in 2020 and 2021.

pain_points.description: Each dispatch is relayed by phone from the desk to a separate control room, adding a hand-off and a chance of mishearing the MW or the unit.

evidence.note: Estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

pain_points.description: Converted coal-to-gas units ramp more slowly and less predictably than purpose-built gas plants, so holding them inside the variance takes close operator attention.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.4, Delivery Requirements for Energy (2023-03-31 administrative version; substantive text from 2020-09-16)
sources.supports: Respond to dispatches with reasonable dispatch protocols, personnel and software; start moving toward the dispatched MW within 10 minutes of the dispatch time; reach steady state within the ramp time plus 40 percent (at least 5 minutes) plus 10 minutes; stay inside the allowable dispatch variance over 10-minute periods; restate within 20 minutes if an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or longer. The revision history shows the 2023 version only aligned drafting with the 2020 text.

sources.title: Information Document 2012-005R, Dispatches (posted 2025-03-12; acknowledgement section unchanged since 2016)
sources.supports: Dispatches are issued in the Automated Dispatch and Messaging System (ADaMS) with asset, Dispatch On or Off, MW and effective time; Section 201.7 subsection 5 requires acknowledgement, done with the Ack Disp button; stand-alone storage and generating assets must hold output within plus or minus 5 MW (200 MW or less) or 10 MW (above 200 MW).

sources.title: MSA Compliance Review 2021 (April 5, 2022)
sources.supports: 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 (437 in 2020), 91 percent self-reported; 75 notices of specified penalty totalling 129,250 CAD; 114 matters under section 203.3 (restatements), 83 under 203.4 (dispatch delivery), 67 under 201.7 (dispatch acknowledgement), 43 under 205.6 and 26 under 205.5 (reserves); 74 percent of matters closed with forbearance; TransAlta entities among those penalised.

assumptions: One case is one dispatch or directive for one asset. Dispatches to the partner-operated unit shares are acknowledged by the desk but delivered by the partner's control room, and are counted in the gas branch without separate partner steps.
The volume of 3,000 a month is the organisation file's estimate; it is the number most worth checking against ADaMS history.
Branch shares (36 percent gas, 47 percent hydro, 6 percent battery or wind, 5 percent reserve directives, 3 percent starts, 3 percent queries) are estimates.

Step resources show the plant being moved during the ramp: the converted unit for 10 to 45 minutes, a hydro plant for 5 to 30 minutes, the battery for 5 to 60 minutes. The plant keeps running afterwards; this only marks the period it is tied to the dispatch change.
Desk relay of dispatches by phone is assumed for 2019-2022; where control rooms watched ADaMS directly the relay step is shorter but still includes a confirmation.

The converted_gas_unit resource is listed without its running cost per hour (14,000 CAD in the organisation file), because fuel and carbon burned during a ramp are the cost of generating energy that the pool pays for, not a cost of handling the dispatch; including it would add about 2,200 CAD to every case.
Wind farm curtailments are rare and are included in the battery branch without a separate wind_farm resource.
The simulated cycle is about 25 to 50 minutes, close to the rule-derived benchmark.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
